a01_p01.tip.en: Three ways to use *sulat*: *ginasulat* (the letter), *ginasulatan* (the person you write to), *sulati!* (write to her!).
a01_p01.tip.fil: Tatlong paraan ng paggamit ng *sulat*: *ginasulat* (ang liham), *ginasulatan* (ang taong sinusulatan mo), *sulati!* (sulatan mo siya!).

a01_p02.terms[1].note.en: the thing is in the spotlight (gin-)

a01_p02.terms[2].note.en: the person written to is in the spotlight (gin-…-an)

a01_p02.text.en: The same event can put three different things in the spotlight. The start and end of the verb tell you which one. Filipino works the same way.
a01_p02.text.fil: Puwedeng maglagay ang iisang pangyayari ng tatlong magkakaibang bagay sa spotlight. Ang simula at dulo ng pandiwa ang nagsasabi kung alin. Ganito rin sa Filipino.

a01_p04.text.en: *-an* changes some spellings: basa → *basahan*. In this lesson, use *ginbuligan* when the person or group being helped is in the spotlight: *Ginbuligan niya si Nanay.*
a01_p04.text.fil: Binabago ng *-an* ang baybay ng ilang salita: basa → *basahan*. Sa araling ito, gamitin ang *ginbuligan* kapag ang tinutulungang tao o grupo ang nasa spotlight: *Ginbuligan niya si Nanay.*

a01_p05.title.en: The Person in the Spotlight: gin-…-an

a01_p06.explain.en: the person who receives is in the spotlight, so the verb takes *gin-…-an*.

a04_p09.text.en: You may hear some Ilonggos say *ho* (from Filipino *po*), for example *Salamat ho*, especially near Manila-speaking areas. It's understood. This app teaches three common ways to show respect: a title, polite *kamo*, and *palihog* for requests.
a04_p09.text.fil: Puwede mong marinig ang ilang Ilonggo na nagsasabi ng *ho* (mula sa *po* ng Filipino), halimbawa *Salamat ho*, lalo na malapit sa mga lugar na Tagalog ang wika. Naiintindihan ito. Tatlong karaniwang paraan ng paggalang ang itinuturo ng app na ito: titulo, magalang na *kamo*, at *palihog* sa pakiusap.

a06_p08.text.en: For finished events, use *nag-*, *gin-* or *na-*. In a past story, *naga-* shows something that was still going on when another thing happened. (Elsewhere *naga-* is also for ongoing and everyday actions.)

a07_p15.text.en: From 2012, many Philippine schools taught the early grades in the children's home language, Hiligaynon included. In 2024 a new law ended that as the main rule. People still debate which is better, so it's a good topic to practise this lesson's moves.

a08_p15.text.fil: Malaking bahagi pa rin ng araw-araw na buhay sa Western Visayas ang AM radio. Nagsimula sa Iloilo ang Bombo Radyo, isa sa pinakamalalaking radio network sa bansa.

a09_p15.text.en: *Dandansoy* is one of the best-known Hiligaynon folk songs, sung in schools all over the Philippines. Songs are the hardest things to translate: you have to keep the meaning, the feeling and the rhythm at the same time.
